CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT

Specimen Type: Fetal tissue (placental)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Analysis of fetal tissue from twin pregnancy
Clinical History: Twin pregnancy

TEST PERFORMED
Oligonucleotide Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)
QF-PCR Analysis for Aneuploidy Detection

METHODOLOGY
Array CGH analysis was performed on uncultured placental DNA using the GenArray-8000 oligonucleotide array platform. This array is designed to detect clinically significant genomic imbalances and any imbalance greater than 1Mb throughout the genome. Analysis was performed using GenScan software with the GRCh37/hg19 human genome reference assembly.

Supplementary QF-PCR (Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction) analysis was performed to specifically exclude triploidy using markers for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y.

RESULTS

ARRAY CGH RESULTS:
arr(1-22,X)x2

Interpretation: Normal female chromosome complement

No copy number variants of clinical significance were detected.
No genomic imbalances >1Mb were identified.

QF-PCR RESULTS:
Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern
Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern
Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern
Chromosome X: Two copies detected
Chromosome Y: Not detected
Triploidy: EXCLUDED

INTERPRETATION
Array CGH analysis of uncultured placental DNA showed no abnormalities. The results are consistent with a normal female chromosome complement with no clinically significant imbalances detected. QF-PCR analysis confirmed the absence of common aneuploidies and excluded triploidy.

LIMITATIONS
- Array CGH cannot detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Low-level mosaicism (<20-30%) may not be detected
- Single gene mutations and methylation abnormalities are not detected by this method
- Uniparental disomy cannot be excluded
- The resolution of this array is limited to imbalances >1Mb

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is required for this sample based on the current findings.
